_about: Where each material may spawn when the world is generated (A2). scripts/spawn_regions.gd reads this.
Materials are named, not numbered. A name the material table does not know yet is skipped, so a
row can be written ahead of the material it names.
Existing features (veins, seams, aquifers, caves, pockets) still come from worldgen.gd and keep each
seed's layout; this table places what is added on top of them.
areas: named places, built before the spawns that use them.
mound: a heap of `fill` standing on the ground beside the anchor. anchor 'hub' is the Hub's middle;
dx = [min, max] cells off it, side picked per seed; width and height are [min, max] cells.
patch: a ragged ellipse inside a home range. x = [min, max] as fractions of the world's width,
depth = [min, max] rows (a depth band), size = [rx, ry] cells. Biomes (A6) are patches.
spawns: one row each.
material: a material name.  area: a name from areas, or 'world' (the default).
x, depth: the home range, as above (area 'world' only; an area brings its own).
host: names it may replace; nothing else is touched.
clumps: [min, max] how many; radius: [min, max] cells; shape: blob (a ragged ellipse) or
speckle (a loose scatter of single cells, `density` 0-1 of the disc). aspect: squashes a blob
into a seam or vein, `radius` cells either way across and radius / aspect up and down.
Wave 1 rows (the second half of the list) follow claude/WAVE1_MATERIALS.md's home table.
Ferrite sits above the Sulfur band (A5): seams in the Ferrite hills and a fourth in the Hub's middle third, so a straight shaft meets one
before the casing needs Plating.
Wave 2 rows (A5 part 3): Brine, Salt and Chlor in the Salt flats, Lumen, Veinstone, Gall and Vitriol in the Gall caverns (A6). Lye, Lift, Pitch, Chillant and Filings are made, not found.
Liquids stay clear of the warm rows: Brine (boils to Salt at 200) is kept above row 2650 and the worldgen caves and water pockets above 2525, where the ambient (D.ambient_at) is still under 100.
Biomes (A6 part 2): a patch with a few more keys. Six of them, two to a band, each about a fifth of the width, on a flank of the world:
anchor: box (the default, a centre anywhere in the range), surface (the centre on the ground) or lava_pocket (the centre of the pocket nearest the flank).
side: random takes a flank per seed (x is written for the left one and mirrors for the right); opposite: <patch> takes the flank that patch did not.
avoid: ['aquifers'] and the like, rectangles the patch tries not to cover.  size: [rx, ry] cells, the rim wobbles by a fifth.

ambient: degrees added to the row's ambient temperature (D.ambient_at) in the biome's chunks, fading to nothing over 40 cells past its rim (`chunk_offsets`; sim.set_ambient_offsets). Keep the sums clear of the thresholds: Water 0 and 100, Brine -15 and 200, Sulfur 600, Coal 700 (scenario_temperature O checks four seeds).

ground: the recipe, rules {from: [names], to: name, density, not_near: [names], gap} tried in order on every cell inside (not_near keeps `gap` cells clear of those); label and color are the biome view's.
A row with `area` set to a patch starts its clumps inside it and cuts them off at its rim (clip: false lets them spill), and may carry a `depth`
to keep to part of the patch. Residents therefore are found there and nowhere else, except the small outliers kept in the Hub's middle third:
Ferrite's fourth seam, a Flux seam and a Rime blob, so level 1 of every Mk upgrade is a straight shaft and the rest send a rig to a flank.
The flanks (centres at 0.13 to 0.20 of the width, or mirrored) keep clear of the middle third. Moving the rows changed the stream, so every
seed's spawned layout differs from A5's.
spring: true puts a spring on the floor of each clump of the row (the Fen's Water pockets, so a Waterwheel has a source that refills; A6 part 4).
enabled: false parks a row.
